title: Your Savings Rate Sets Your Retirement Date

beats.say: Save ten percent of your pay, and it takes about fifty one years to reach financial independence. Save fifty percent, and it takes about seventeen.
beats.visual: a long winding road stretching to a distant horizon in morning mist, wide shot, no people

beats.say: This is an illustration, not a promise. We assume a five percent return after inflation.
beats.visual: an old brass calculator beside a stack of ledgers under a green banker lamp, no people

beats.say: We also assume you need twenty five times your yearly spending saved.
beats.visual: a tall stack of twenty five gold coins on a dark table, dramatic side light

beats.say: Here is the math. Every year, you save a slice of your pay.
beats.visual: a single seed on bare soil in soft window light, macro, no people

beats.say: Save ten percent, and you spend ninety. The target is big and the savings are small.
beats.visual: a very tall mountain with a tiny trail climbing it at dawn, wide shot, no people

beats.say: It takes about fifty one years.
beats.visual: an hourglass nearly full of sand on a dark wooden table, hard side light

beats.say: Save twenty five percent, and it takes about thirty two years.
beats.visual: a long staircase winding up a quiet hillside in morning light, no people

beats.say: Save fifty percent, and you spend half. The target is half as big, and you fill it twice as fast.
beats.visual: two stacks of gold coins, one half the height of the other, black marble, dramatic light

beats.say: That is about seventeen years. Save sixty five percent, and it is about ten and a half.
beats.visual: a short bridge crossing a narrow stream at sunrise, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Your savings rate does two jobs. It fills the pot and shrinks the target.
beats.visual: a funnel of golden light pouring into a small glass jar in a dark room

beats.say: The honest catch: real returns bounce around, and saving fifty percent is not possible for everyone.
beats.visual: a stormy sea with waves rising and falling under a heavy sky and a lighthouse

beats.say: So treat it as direction, not a prediction. Each extra percent moves the finish line closer.
beats.visual: a single stone step leading up a long quiet staircase into morning mist, no people

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: Saving 10% of pay: about 51 years to financial independence. Saving 50%: about 17. A 5% real return and 25x spending assumed. An illustration, not a promise. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: How long until you can stop working depends more on how much of your pay you save than on what you earn. At a 5 percent real return and 25 times spending, saving 10 percent takes about 51 years and saving 50 percent about 17. An illustration, not a promise.
first_comment: What is your savings rate right now? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: Years to reach 25x annual spending, saving s of pay each year at a 5% real return: 10% = about 51 years, 25% = about 32, 50% = about 17, 65% = about 10.5
25x annual spending corresponds to the 4% withdrawal guideline
Assumptions: spending constant, no taxes, steady real return; real life varies
